stem: An 8-year-old boy is brought in by his mother after about three weeks of cough and reduced energy. He recently changed schools, and his mother wonders whether the adjustment is affecting his appetite and mood. He has no significant past medical history. No known TB contact in the household. No prior TB treatment, no known drug-resistant contact. Sputum obtained with coaching was scant, so a gastric aspirate was also collected; it returned positive for M. tuberculosis on molecular testing. Exam: mild wasting, faint left-sided crackles, no lymphadenopathy.

patient.social_history: Lives with mother; recently changed schools
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough, reduced energy, reduced appetite attributed initially to adjusting to a new school
patient.exam_findings: Mild wasting, faint left-sided crackles, no lymphadenopathy
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: The school change proposed as the primary explanation for his reduced appetite and mood, delaying recognition of a physical illness
His reduced energy attributed to normal adjustment stress rather than a persistent physical process
ntep_correct_actions: Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
Do not order mycobacterial culture as a routine parallel test alongside the initial molecular test; reserve culture for the downstream resistance-testing cascade after a positive molecular result.
Dose first-line anti-TB drugs using a fixed-dose-combination tablet count assigned by the patient's weight band, not a per-kilogram calculation performed at the point of care.

us_correct_actions: Reserve rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for patients who meet at least one specific risk criterion (prior TB treatment, birth in or residence in a higher-TB-incidence country, contact with a known MDR-TB case, or HIV infection); do not order it routinely for a patient with none of these risk factors.
Send both liquid and solid mycobacterial culture on the initial specimen regardless of the molecular test result, since culture is considered the gold-standard microbiologic test.
Calculate this patient's anti-TB drug doses individually in mg/kg based on current body weight, rather than assigning a fixed tablet count by weight band.
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance testing because no specific household contact with TB was identified
expected_divergence_points: Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is ordered universally or only for patients meeting specific US risk criteria
Whether mycobacterial culture is ordered as a mandatory parallel test or reserved for the resistance-detection cascade
Whether drug dosing is assigned via a weight-band FDC tablet count or calculated individually in mg/kg
